q: What is the minimum investment for PMS?
a: ₹50 lakh, which is the regulatory minimum for any portfolio management service in India. You can bring cash, existing shares, or both.
Yes. Unlike a mutual fund, where you own units of a pool, PMS shares sit in a demat account in your own name. You can see every holding.

A fixed fee of 2% a year, charged monthly, and a performance fee of 20% only on returns above a 10% hurdle, with a high-water mark. If you withdraw within the first year there is a 1.5% exit load. Operating expenses are capped at 0.1%.
You receive a monthly statement with every holding and transaction, quarterly reviews with the team, and a 24/7 client portal.

As you own the shares directly, gains are taxed in your hands as capital gains on each sale, long-term or short-term depending on holding period. Dividends are taxed as income. We provide tax-ready statements; please consult your tax adviser.
Usually 7 to 10 working days once documents are in. Our Compliance Officer works with the custodian on the account opening; your relationship manager keeps you informed at each step.

q: Can I exit whenever I want?
a: Yes. PMS is open-ended. Withdrawals within the first year carry a 1.5% exit load; after that there is none.

q: Will you tell me what you hold before I invest?
a: We share sector and market-cap allocation and the FAITH framework before you invest, and full stock-level disclosure every month after. Pre-investment non-disclosure protects the strategy for existing clients.

q: What is the minimum to start?
a: ₹5,000 a month through a SIP, or a one-time lumpsum. Many clients begin smaller than they expected and scale up.

We distribute regular plans and are paid a commission by the fund house; direct plans are available from the fund house without one. What you pay us for is selection, allocation and the discipline to stay invested.

q: What do I need for KYC?
a: PAN, Aadhaar, a bank account and a photograph. Most KYC is completed online in a day.

Equity funds held over a year are taxed as long-term capital gains above the annual exemption; under a year, short-term. Debt funds are taxed at your slab. Rules change; we will tell you when they do.

q: Can I stop or pause a SIP?
a: Yes, at any time, without penalty. ELSS investments have a three-year lock-in per instalment.
